cues.zh: 在登山界声誉无可挑剔。后来我们找到了一个叫 Bruce Norman 的人，他也从未登顶过 8000 米级山峰。但他在探索性登山方面非常有名，

cues.en: and I've known him for about a dozen years. So it seemed like we had a really good team. It seemed like if nothing else, we could come together and agree on a couple of goals. And our first goal was everybody had to get home alive. Right? Our second goal was that we all wanted to summit. And our third goal is we wanted to do it in a style that represented who we were as people, that really showed off the best of what we believe mountaineering to be. So we went off to the mountain. We got there on June 1.
cues.zh: 我认识他大概有十二年了。所以看起来我们凑出了一支很不错的队伍。看起来至少我们能聚到一起，就几个目标达成一致。我们的第一个目标是所有人都必须活着回家。对吧？第二个目标是我们都想登顶。第三个目标是，我们要以一种能代表我们是什么样的人的方式去完成，真正展现出我们心目中登山最美好的一面。于是我们就出发去那座山了。我们在 6 月 1 日到达。

cues.en: That K2 is being K2, sending down these gigantic avalanches.
cues.zh: K2就是K2，正倾泻下这些巨大的雪崩。

cues.en: We placed base camp
cues.zh: 我们把大本营设在

cues.en: on this glacier here at 17,200
cues.zh: 这片冰川上，海拔17,200

cues.en: feet. From there we have to march up the glacier through the ice falls to access this side of K2.
cues.zh: 英尺。从那里，我们得沿冰川向上，穿过冰瀑，才能到达K2的这一侧。

cues.en: On the second day of the expedition we almost die the first time. Bruce and I are tied together by a rope. We're passing through this gigantic ice fall. And as he's walking across a snow bridge, he's walking across what seems like a completely flat section of snow, suddenly the floor gives out on him and he goes shooting 25 feet down into this hole, this gigantic crevasse. Now, crevasse could be two fifty feet to 500 feet deep and he's rocketing down in there. He's tied to me by a rope. Suddenly that rope comes tight and I'm in a tug of war. I know I'm going to lose. And I'm being dragged towards the lip of this crevasse. The two of us are going to be rocket down to the bottom. We'll just be entombed in ice. Within an hour or two, we will die, and they will never be able to find our bodies. And as I'm sliding across, knowing I'm going to die, suddenly the ground underneath me
cues.zh: 探险第二天，我们第一次差点死掉。Bruce和我被一根绳子系在一起。我们正穿过巨大的冰瀑。他走过一座雪桥，走在看起来完全平坦的雪面上，突然脚下塌了，他一下子坠入25英尺深的洞里，一个巨大的冰裂缝。冰裂缝可能有两百五十到五百英尺深，他正飞速往下掉。他和我系在同一根绳子上。突然绳子绷紧，我像在拔河。我知道我赢不了，正被拖向冰裂缝边缘。我们俩会一起坠到底，葬身冰中。一两个小时内我们就会死，他们永远找不到我们的遗体。就在我滑过去、知道自己要死的时候，突然我脚下的地面

cues.en: explodes open, and I fall in a separate crevasse. And Bruce is 25 feet down in one hole, and I'm five feet down in the other. Right? So it was a pure miracle. Right? It was just I'm still blown away by that. In fact, looking at the history of mountaineering, never before
cues.zh: 突然裂开，我掉进了另一个冰裂缝。Bruce 在其中一个洞里，往下25英尺；我在另一个洞里，往下5英尺。对吧？这简直是纯粹的奇迹。对吧？我到现在都觉得难以置信。事实上，纵观登山史，从未有过——

cues.en: have two people fallen into two different crevasses at exactly the same time. Right? Normally, both fall in the same crevasse, as I said, they just put a little take your dinner plate and
cues.zh: 两个人恰好在同一时刻掉进两个不同的冰裂缝。对吧？通常两人会掉进同一个冰裂缝，就像我说的，他们只是拿个小牌子，把你的

cues.en: type your name into it and hang it on the rock. Well, we started up the mountain. We made actually four different attempts through June and into July. And each time we would be stopped by the horrendous snowstorms that are typical in this part of the world. We would climb in the snowstorms quite often because we knew we had to force our way up. We had to get 500 pounds of equipment into place, you know, tents and sleeping bags and stoves and ropes and all sorts of other stuff. We had established the camps, we had all this work to do. Just pure labor when you're on a mountaineering expedition. Know, comes up with a great idea, it sounds like a lot of fun at home, and then you get there and you find out it's nothing but brutally difficult work. We would push no matter what the weather was, so we would be out in, a blizzard, wind blowing 40 miles an hour, temperatures of minus 20.
cues.zh: 名字写上去，再挂在岩石上。好，我们开始登山。从六月到七月，我们实际尝试了四次。每次都被这一带常见的可怕暴风雪拦住。我们经常在暴风雪中攀登，因为我们知道必须硬闯上去。我们得把500磅装备运到位，你知道，帐篷、睡袋、炉子、绳索等各种东西。我们要建营地，有这么多活要干。登山探险就是纯粹的苦力活。你知道，想出个好主意，在家里听起来很有趣，到了那里才发现只有残酷艰难的劳作。无论天气如何我们都往前推，所以会在暴风雪里，风速每小时40英里，气温零下20度。

cues.en: Sometimes we would stay out there as long as we could, past the point when we would run out of food. I don't know if you guys have ever had a stale bread and goose sandwich before, but it's not the most you know, culinary
cues.zh: 有时候我们会尽量在外面待久一点，甚至待到食物都吃完之后。我不知道你们有没有吃过放硬的面包夹鹅肉三明治，但它真不是最——你懂的——烹饪

cues.en: thing. You can see the look on their faces, how desperate this meal is going to be. We pushed our way up to Camp 3. We got all way up to 24,500
cues.zh: 上的东西。你能从他们脸上看出来，这顿饭会有多绝望。我们一路推进到3号营地。我们一直上到24,500

cues.en: feet. And at this point, things really slowed down for us. The snow was deeper than waist deep. And we tried. We tried really hard to push our way up. We never could figure out a way. We couldn't make it. We physically couldn't, didn't have enough
cues.zh: 英尺。到这时，我们的进度真的慢下来了。雪深过腰。我们试了。我们非常努力想往上推进。我们始终找不到办法。我们上不去。我们体力上做不到，没有足够的

cues.en: labor or enough push to be able to break the trail through this deep of snow. We would go out, we would maybe make 100 or 200 feet of progress in a day, and that was it. And finally, we decided it was physically impossible for a team of three to be able to pull this off. So we came all the way back down to base camp. Now we were not the only team that was working on the mountain at the same time. There was a strong Russian team. There was a strong Korean team. There was a team of Italians who arrived late who were not as strong. There was an Iranian climber, and there was two Portuguese climbers.
cues.zh: 劳力，也没有足够的推进力，能在这 么深的雪里开路。我们出去一天，可能只能前进100或200英尺，就这样。最后我们认定，三个人组成的队伍在体力上不可能完成这件事。于是我们一路撤回大本营。当时山上不止我们一支队伍。有一支很强的俄罗斯队。有一支很强的韩国队。有一支晚到的意大利队，没那么强。有一名伊朗登山者，还有两名葡萄牙登山者。

cues.en: They were also trying the same thing. But for some reason none of us were on the same sequence, the same schedule, right?
cues.zh: 他们也在尝试同样的事。但不知为什么，我们谁都没处在同一序列、同一进度上，对吧？

cues.en: Mainly because most people wanted somebody else to do the hard work. So everyone always tried to stay one camp below, right? So, well, the Russians got to Camp 3 and they also failed to make it higher. The Koreans got to Camp 3, they also failed to make it higher. We got to Camp 3, we failed to make it higher. And once everyone had experienced that failure,
cues.zh: 主要是因为大多数人都想让别人去干苦活。所以每个人总想待低一个营地，对吧？结果，俄罗斯人到了 Camp 3，也没能上得更高。韩国人到了 Camp 3，也没能上得更高。我们到了 Camp 3，也没能上得更高。而一旦每个人都经历过这种失败，

cues.en: we knew we could then have a conversation about cooperation.
cues.zh: 我们就知道，那时可以谈谈合作了。

cues.en: We've So got everyone together back in base camp. It's now the middle of July. We know we only have maybe one, at most two more attempts left in us before the season is going to close, and if we don't come together now to make a
cues.zh: 我们把所有人都召集回了大本营。现在是七月中旬。我们知道，在登山季结束之前，我们大概只剩一次、最多两次尝试机会了，如果我们现在不齐心协力发起一次

cues.en: concerted summit bid, we don't stand a chance.
cues.zh: 共同的冲顶行动，我们就毫无机会。

cues.en: So we have all the team leaders come together and we create a plan.
cues.zh: 于是我们把所有队长召集到一起，制定了一个计划。

cues.en: And the plan is, you know, it's a high
cues.zh: 这个计划呢，你知道，细节非常

cues.en: level of detail to it, but it's pretty basically simple. We'll all go together, Right? And we will all leave based on weather forecasts that our team is getting because they seem very reliable.
cues.zh: 详尽，但基本上很简单。我们一起上，对吧？我们会根据团队拿到的天气预报出发，因为那些预报看起来非常可靠。

cues.en: And the plan is that we're going to leave on the morning of the July 15. For us, it's our fifth attempt on the mountain. We have now been away from home for
cues.zh: 计划是我们7月15日早上出发。对我们来说，这是第五次挑战这座山。我们现在已经离家

cues.en: about sixty days. So we've been out for a long period of time, and here we are heading up the mountain.
cues.zh: 大约六十天了。所以我们出来很久了，现在我们正往山上走。

cues.en: We're leaving base camp about 05:30 in the morning
cues.zh: 我们大约早上5点30分离开大本营

cues.en: or 06:30 in the morning.
cues.zh: 或者早上6点30分。

cues.en: Alright. Ready to get our butts hooked again? Yep. Ready to step on the beast.
cues.zh: 好了。准备好再挂上保护绳了吗？准备好了。准备好踏上这头野兽了。

cues.en: Here we go. It's our first step.
cues.zh: 开始了。这是我们的第一步。

cues.en: Pretty nice up there, Yeah.
cues.zh: 上面还挺不错，嗯。

cues.en: Well, here we are back on our way up K 2. We're below
cues.zh: 好了，我们又踏上了攀登K2的路。我们现在在

cues.en: Camp 1. And sure enough, it's snowing
cues.zh: 1号营地下面。果然，又下雪了

cues.en: and blowing on us again.
cues.zh: 风又朝我们刮过来了。

cues.en: This mountain bluffs are torturous.
cues.zh: 这座山的峭壁真折磨人。

cues.en: Certainly
cues.zh: 确实，

cues.en: never given us the easy way out.
cues.zh: 它从没让我们轻松过。

cues.en: Beautiful Camp 1 again. We
cues.zh: 又见到美丽的1号营地。我们

cues.en: got up this orange and we looked up onto the black pyramid towards Camp 2. There was just a number of clouds ripping across the base.
cues.zh: 爬上了这片橙色地带，抬头望向通往2号营地的黑色金字塔。只有几团云正掠过山脚。

cues.en: We were alone. There's no one else with us. And so we kinda talked to each other and we all decided, let's just go for it.
cues.zh: 我们当时孤身一人，身边没有别人。于是我们互相聊了聊，大家决定，那就上吧。

cues.en: This is the funnel right here.
cues.zh: 这就是那个漏斗区。

cues.en: This is probably the worst place
cues.zh: 这大概是最糟糕的地方

cues.en: to be in conditions like this.
cues.zh: 尤其是在这种条件下。

cues.en: I can only go through this section
cues.zh: 我只能通过这一段

cues.en: one at a time.
cues.zh: 一次一个人。

cues.en: It's just too dangerous.
cues.zh: 实在太危险了。

cues.en: Here we are at 26,000 feet and the
cues.zh: 我们现在在26,000英尺的高度，而

cues.en: weather's just
cues.zh: 天气简直

cues.en: not cooperating at all.
cues.zh: 完全不配合。

cues.en: Don is doing a great job of breaking trail for us. Days like this really went down.
cues.zh: Don 为我们开路做得很好。这样的日子真是难熬。

cues.en: Snow conditions are just horrendous and
cues.zh: 雪况简直糟透了，而且

cues.en: looked like the wind died about an hour and a half ago.
cues.zh: 风看起来在大约一个半小时前停了。

cues.en: It's one of those days when you
cues.zh: 就是那种日子，你会

cues.en: wish you took up golf and set them out here and
cues.zh: 恨不得自己当初去打高尔夫，把球打到这儿来，而且

cues.en: I will just
cues.zh: 我就只能

cues.en: find Camp 3 somehow
cues.zh: 想办法找到三号营地

cues.en: and then
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: probably four hours before we roll our sleeping bag over.
cues.zh: 大概还要四个小时，我们才能把睡袋铺开。

cues.en: We're at Camp 3. I'll tell you, it took us about two and a half hours to send that last 100 meters or so. Without exaggeration,
cues.zh: 我们到三号营地了。跟你说，最后那100米左右，我们花了大约两个半小时才完攀。毫不夸张，

cues.en: you couldn't touch bottom.
cues.zh: 你根本踩不到底。

cues.en: And... But we did get here. We're all comfortable.
cues.zh: 而且……但我们确实到这儿了。大家都还行。

cues.en: With boiling water.
cues.zh: 还有开水。

cues.en: And we'll head for Camp 4 tomorrow.
cues.zh: 明天我们就向4号营地进发。

cues.en: The only problem with getting to Camp 3 was that nobody else came with us. Right? So that was the plan. All the teams would come together. We'd all make this gigantic rush. Well, they all rolled over that first morning when they saw there was snow and went back to bed. So here we are at Camp 3. We have waist deep snow ahead of us. We are desperate to get to the summit. We have no choice but to make a push by ourselves. So the next morning we get up and it is a crystal clear beautiful day and we start to move up through this deep snow. And it took us a while to break trail.
cues.zh: 到达3号营地唯一的遗憾，就是没有别人跟我们一起上来。对吧？本来计划是这样的：所有队伍会会合，大家一起发起这场大规模冲顶。结果第一天早上他们看到下雪，全缩回去了，又回去睡觉了。所以现在我们在3号营地，前面是齐腰深的雪。我们非常想登顶，别无选择，只能靠自己冲一把。第二天早上我们起来，天气晴朗通透，美极了，我们开始穿过深雪往上走。开路花了我们不少时间。

cues.en: In fact, we were going so slow that people who were a day behind us were eventually able to catch up to us, right? So they climbed all way up to Camp 2, up to Camp 3, and then some people moved from Camp 3 up towards us. And they couldn't believe how slow the progress was until they got in front of us. So here comes the Portuguese, they're like, come on, you guys can go faster. And we're like, why don't you give us some help? And they're like, great. So they rushed ahead and they took 10 steps and they said, this is impossible. We should camp here. And they were right. So we put up a camp 400 or 500 feet above where everybody else is camping at Camp 3. We called it Camp 3.5.
cues.zh: 事实上，我们走得实在太慢，落后我们一天路程的人最后居然都能追上我们，对吧？于是一路爬到 Camp 2，再到 Camp 3，然后有些人从 Camp 3 朝我们这边上来。直到走到我们前面，他们才相信我们的进度有多慢。这时葡萄牙队来了，他们说：拜托，你们可以走快点啊。我们说：那你们怎么不帮帮忙？他们说：行啊。于是他们冲到前面，走了 10 步就说：这不可能，我们得在这儿扎营。他们说得没错。于是我们在其他人扎营的 Camp 3 上方四五百英尺处建了个营地，叫它 Camp 3.5。

cues.en: So here we are at Camp 3.5, and we're getting ready to push on to Camp 4.
cues.zh: 现在我们到了3.5号营地，正准备向4号营地推进。

cues.en: And if you could crank the sound up, because the louder the better, I think.
cues.zh: 能不能把声音调大点，我觉得越响越好。

cues.en: Here we are at 7,700
cues.zh: 我们现在位于海拔7700

cues.en: meters inside of our Camp 3.5.
cues.zh: 米，就在我们的3.5号营地里。

cues.en: It was quite an amazing place underneath this giant tower of ice.
cues.zh: 在这座巨大冰塔下面，这地方真挺震撼。

cues.en: There's the team
cues.zh: 队伍在那儿

cues.en: getting ready to leave camp.
cues.zh: 正准备离开营地。

cues.en: What do you reckon our follow-up progress is?
cues.zh: 你估计我们接下来的前进速度是多少？

cues.en: Three meters per hour? Not very much.
cues.zh: 每小时三米？不太多。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是啊。

cues.en: Good
cues.zh: 不错

cues.en: feel, Bruce. Alright.
cues.zh: 的感觉，Bruce。好的。

cues.en: Diet. Happy.
cues.zh: 饮食。开心。

cues.en: And ecstatic at the view. You
cues.zh: 而且对着这景色欣喜若狂。你

cues.en: just can't sit on top of the waddle because of that thing.
cues.zh: 就是没法坐在 waddle 顶上，因为那东西。

cues.en: Well, that thing that Bruce is talking about is the the final 2,500
cues.zh: Bruce 说的那个东西，就是最后 2,500

cues.en: feet of the climb. So when we leave here, and our plan is to leave here between 10:30 and 11:30 at night,
cues.zh: 英尺的攀登段。我们离开这里时，计划是在晚上 10:30 到 11:30 之间从这里出发，

cues.en: we'll walk across this section called the shoulder. This is all above 26, it's about 26 and a half to almost 27,000
cues.zh: 我们会穿过这段叫“肩部”的区域。这一段都在 26,000 以上，大约 26,500 到接近 27,000

cues.en: feet. Then we climb into this section here called the Bottleneck, and that is a really steep gully, maybe up to 55 degrees steep. And then at the top of that, we traverse under this hanging glacier. This glacier here is over 500 feet thick, and it's dangerous in two ways. One is pieces of it are constantly coming down. And the second thing is that it becomes almost vertical as you climb across here, so it's very difficult climbing. And then we'll go around the corner, and then we'll be able to scurry from there to the summit. We think it's going to take us at least twelve hours to get to the top. In fact, your average summit day on K2 is twenty two hours long. You would love to be able to summit 09:00,
cues.zh: 英尺。然后我们爬进这里这段叫 Bottleneck（瓶颈）的区域，那是一个非常陡的沟槽，坡度可能达到 55 度。到了那上面，我们从这条悬冰川下方横切。这条冰川有 500 多英尺厚，危险有两方面。一是不断有碎冰掉落。二是你在这里横切时，它几乎成了垂直的，所以攀爬非常困难。然后我们会绕过转角，从那里快速冲向顶峰。我们认为至少需要十二个小时才能登顶。事实上，在 K2 上，平均冲顶日长达 22 小时。你会很想能在 9:00 登顶，

cues.en: 10:00, 11:00 in the morning, so you have all day to be able to come back down. It tends to be on mountaineering that most of the accidents happen on the descent. So what we'd love to be able to do is to descend in daylight,
cues.zh: 早上10点、11点，这样你有一整天时间下撤。登山时大多数事故往往发生在下撤途中。所以我们希望能做到在白天光线好时下撤，

cues.en: descend in the warmth of the sun, especially because our team is not using oxygen, right. So without that extra oxygen, it really saps away more than anything else. It makes you colder. And we want all, every advantage to get back down alive. In fact, we don't even want to stay at Camp 4 that night if we can. We would love to descend all way to Camp 3, because there's very little protection from storms at Camp 4. So that's the plan when we get there. Now we
cues.zh: 在太阳的温暖中下撤，尤其因为我们队不用氧气，对吧。没有额外的氧气，它会比什么都更消耗你。它会让你更冷。我们要争取一切优势，活着下撤。事实上，如果可以，我们甚至不想那晚留在4号营地。我们很想一路下撤到3号营地，因为4号营地对风暴几乎没有防护。这就是我们到那里后的计划。现在我们

cues.en: had hoped that everybody would join us. Eventually they did. We were carrying the 3,000 feet of ropes, the ice screws, the pitons, all the other stuff they needed to fix the ropes for summit day. cues.en: pushing up. This is Stefano Zavka, who at 09:30... This is him at 09:30 in the morning.
cues.zh: 正奋力往上爬。这是 Stefano Zavka，在09:30……这是早上9:30的他。

cues.en: His team thinks he's gone down, but it continues going up. This
cues.zh: 他的团队以为他已经下撤了，但他还在继续往上。这

cues.en: is the Italian base camp just finding out that Daniele Nardia has summoned K 2.
cues.zh: 是意大利大本营刚刚得知 Daniele Nardia 已经登顶 K2 的画面。

cues.en: So their expedition is now a success.
cues.zh: 所以他们的探险现在算成功了。

cues.en: There's Daniele at the top. They have no idea that two other members of the four person team are still going up.
cues.zh: Daniele 就在顶峰。他们完全不知道，四人队伍中的另外两名成员还在往上走。

cues.en: Every time I see that, I want to cry. Here
cues.zh: 每次看到那个画面，我都想哭。此刻

cues.en: we are descending from the summit.
cues.zh: 我们正从顶峰下撤。

cues.en: We're on the fixed lines now. Remember, there's 3,000 feet of rope that we put out. We were descending down.
cues.zh: 我们现在在固定路绳上。记住，我们铺设了 3000 英尺的绳索。我们当时正在下撤。

cues.en: We needed to get to this point here where we disconnect from the line so we can walk back to camp.
cues.zh: 我们得走到这个位置，从路绳上脱开，才能走回营地。

cues.en: at night, Don and I are getting to the ends of the rope. The Czech climber has gone on ahead of us. It's pitch black dark. There's so much clouds over the sky, there's not a star in the sky.
cues.zh: 夜里，Don 和我快到绳子尽头了。那个捷克攀登者已经走到我们前面。四周漆黑一片。天上云层很厚，一颗星星也看不到。

cues.en: And Don is walking past an object that he thinks is a plastic garbage bag, and it says to him, help me, I'm dying.
cues.zh: Don 走过一个他以为是塑料垃圾袋的东西，那东西对他说：救救我，我要死了。

cues.en: And it's the check climber. He's gotten himself down to the end of the ropes where he collapsed. He has no idea where to go. He's suffering from cerebral edema, hypothermia.
cues.zh: 是那个捷克登山者。他沿着路绳下到尽头，倒在那里。他完全不知道该往哪走。他出现了脑水肿和失温。

cues.en: We lift him up, he walks 50 feet and collapses. We lift him up again, he walks 20 feet and collapses. We're over a thousand feet from camp. We put him over our shoulders and literally start to drag this man for over an hour to try to bring him back to our campsite. We can't get him to his camp for it, it's too far away, we don't even know where his tent is. So we drag him into our tent, we send Bruce out ahead to try to start making water for us, we get into the tent, we send Don in first, we send
cues.zh: 我们把他扶起来，他走了50英尺就倒下。再扶起来，他走了20英尺又倒下。我们离营地有一千多英尺。我们把他架到肩上，真的拖着这个人走了一个多小时，想把他带回我们的营地。我们没法把他送回他的营地，太远了，我们甚至不知道他的帐篷在哪。所以我们把他拖进我们的帐篷。我们先让Bruce出去，试着给大家烧水。我们进了帐篷，先把Don送进去，再送

cues.en: Libor in second. We have no sleeping bag for a fourth person, so I give up my sleeping bag so Libor can be warmed up. There's a three person tent, we're going to try to cram four people into it. It's not really a pleasant thought to climb in there. So I'm standing outside the tent for as long as I possibly can. And I go over to the Italian tent, I start to ask the Italian leader Daniele, who's been down for hours, right, resting in his tent. Daniele, have you heard from Mario and Stefano? No, Chris. They won't call me on their radio. And I look up the mountain and I could see their lights together on the Traverse.
cues.zh: Libor第二个进去。我们没有第四个睡袋，所以我把自己的睡袋让出来，让Libor暖和过来。那是个三人帐，我们打算硬塞四个人进去。想到要钻进去，实在不太舒服。所以我在帐篷外尽量多站一会儿。然后我走到意大利队的帐篷，问意大利队队长Daniele——他已经下撤好几个小时了，正在帐篷里休息。Daniele，有Mario和Stefano的消息吗？没有，Chris。他们不肯用无线电呼我。我抬头往山上看，能看到他们的灯光一起在Traverse上。

cues.en: So they're at least three hours away. So you know what, Daniele? They should be back here around midnight. If they're not back here by midnight, come and get me and we will rescue these guys. He says, Okay, Chris, great idea.
cues.zh: 所以他们至少还有三小时路程。这样吧，Daniele？他们应该午夜左右回到这里。如果午夜还没回来，就来找我，我们去救他们。他说：好，Chris，好主意。
于是到了11点
或者11点半，

cues.en: Mario calls into the camp. Daniele, I'm lost. Give me directions. Daniele gives him directions. He gets to tent at 01:00 in the morning. He climbs into the tent. Remember these eyes, in case you ever meet this guy in a dark alley. He says, Daniele... He climbs into the tent next to Daniele. Mario,
cues.zh: Mario呼叫营地。Daniele，我迷路了。给我指路。Daniele给他指了路。他凌晨1点到了帐篷。他爬进帐篷。记住这双眼睛，万一你哪天在暗巷里遇到这家伙。他说：Daniele……他爬进Daniele旁边的帐篷。Mario，

cues.en: where is Stefano? Oh, he's right behind me. Let's lay down and rest. They lay down and fall asleep.
cues.zh: Stefano在哪儿？哦，他就在我后面。我们躺下休息吧。他们躺下睡着了。

cues.en: 03:00 in the morning.
cues.zh: 凌晨3点。

cues.en: Mario, Mario, where is Stefano? I don't know. Go find him. So Mario gets outside the tent to go look for Stefano. Daniele goes back to sleep.
cues.zh: Mario，Mario，Stefano在哪？我不知道。去找他。于是Mario出了帐篷去找Stefano。Daniele又睡着了。

cues.en: Right? We are
cues.zh: 对吧？我们就在

cues.en: six feet away. They never come and tell us that Stefano is missing. Then Mario goes out. We don't know if he went out for five minutes or fifteen minutes, but he comes back into the tent. This time he's very quiet, so he doesn't have to wake up Daniele.
cues.zh: 六英尺外。他们从没过来告诉我们Stefano不见了。然后Mario出去了。我们不知道他出去了五分钟还是十五分钟，但他回到了帐篷里。这次他很安静，这样就不用吵醒Daniele。

cues.en: They go back to sleep. 07:00
cues.zh: 他们又睡了过去。07:00

cues.en: in the morning now. We have no sign of Stefano.
cues.zh: 天亮了，还是不见Stefano的踪影。

cues.en: A blizzard has hit K2.
cues.zh: 一场暴风雪袭击了K2。

cues.en: And the thing that happens at
cues.zh: 而在这种地方会发生的事情是

cues.en: this altitude,
cues.zh: 在这样的海拔，

cues.en: when these blizzards hit,
cues.zh: 当这种暴风雪来袭时，

cues.en: your very chance for survival is extremely limited. In fact, in 1986,
cues.zh: 你生还的机会极其渺茫。事实上，1986年，

cues.en: at the same Camp 4, seven people made the summit, they came back down to Camp 4, they got trapped in a blizzard that night, they said, you know what, we'll wait a day. Let's rest, let's regain our strength, let's wait for the winds to blow the storm out, and then we'll descend tomorrow.
cues.zh: 就在同一个四号营地，七个人登顶后回到四号营地，当晚被困在暴风雪里，他们说，这样吧，我们等一天。先休息，恢复体力，等风把暴风雪吹散，明天再下撤。

cues.en: That day the first person died in her sleeping bag.
cues.zh: 那天，第一个人死在了自己的睡袋里。

cues.en: The leader of the team goes around to these two different tents, three different tents, checking on everybody, sees the one woman dead.
cues.zh: 队长挨个到那两三顶帐篷查看每个人，发现那名女子已经死了。

cues.en: Her partner is in a coma. Right? So they've just, their bodies have given up the fight. He says we have to go down, five of them are left. They start to leave camp, they're descending from Camp 4, they go about a 100 meters below Camp 4,
cues.zh: 她的搭档昏迷了。对吧？他们的身体已经放弃了挣扎。他说我们必须下去，只剩五个人了。他们开始撤离营地，从4号营地往下撤，下到4号营地以下约100米处，

cues.en: two people of the five sit down and die.
cues.zh: 五个人里有两个人坐下后就死了。

cues.en: Right? They're so completely exhausted they can't will themselves to move any further.
cues.zh: 对吧？他们已彻底精疲力尽，连挪动一步的意志都没有了。

cues.en: They continue to ascend somewhere between Camp 3 and Camp 1, one of the three people disappears.
cues.zh: 他们继续在3号营地和1号营地之间的某处向上攀登，三个人中有一人失踪了。

cues.en: Two of seven
cues.zh: 七人中的两人

cues.en: make it off the mountain alive. This is the stuff that you as a student of K2, as someone who's climbing it, has memorized.
cues.zh: 活着下了山。这就是你作为K2研究者、作为攀登K2的人早已熟记于心的东西。

cues.en: Oh my god, we're stuck in Camp 4 in a blizzard after summoning.
cues.zh: 天啊，我们登顶后被困在暴风雪中的4号营地。

cues.en: We will die like the nineteen eighty six team. We have to get ourselves out of here. The Portuguese climber is running around, let's go, let's go, let's go. He takes off, he takes off with the Russians, he takes off with the Koreans, leaves us with Libor, leaves us with the Italians, leaves us with the Iranians to help get those guys down. The Italians get completely dressed, They leave their tent. They try to follow in the footsteps of the Russians. His footsteps have already blown over. They get totally lost. They come back up to the tents. Come on, Chris. Let's go. Let's go. You need to leave now. Like, we're not ready to leave. We're dealing with Libor. He's, you know, having these anxiety attacks. He barely can walk. We need to treat his issue before we can get him off the mountain. Like, no, you have to leave now. It is so dangerous. It's so dangerous the fact that Stefano is dead.
cues.zh: 我们会像1986年那支队伍一样死掉。我们必须离开这里。那个葡萄牙攀登者到处乱跑，走啊，走啊，走啊。他出发了，跟着俄罗斯人走了，跟着韩国人走了，把Libor留给我们，把意大利人留给我们，把伊朗人留给我们去帮忙把那些人弄下山。意大利人穿好全套装备，离开帐篷。他们想跟着俄罗斯人的脚印走。可他的脚印早被风吹没了。他们彻底迷路了。又回到帐篷那里。来吧，Chris。走啊。走啊。你现在必须离开。可我们还没准备好走。我们在处理Libor的情况。他，你知道，正焦虑发作。他几乎走不了路。我们得先处理他的问题，才能把他弄下山。不行，你现在就得走。太危险了。Stefano都死了，这太危险了。

cues.en: They tell us this at 08:30 in the morning. Stefano had been left outside by himself all night in this horrible blizzard.
cues.zh: 他们在早上8:30才告诉我们这件事。Stefano 被独自留在外面，在那场可怕的暴风雪里待了一整夜。

cues.en: He didn't even have a radio.
cues.zh: 他甚至连无线电都没有。

cues.en: Right? So the Italians had
cues.zh: 对吧？所以意大利人那边有

cues.en: four guys in the mountain, but they only had two radios. Mario, when he left Stefano, took the radio with him so he could call down and ask for directions and left Stefano up there on his own in a weakened state to try to find his own way down. Right? Impossible task.
cues.zh: 四个人在山上，但他们只有两台无线电。Mario 离开 Stefano 时，把无线电带走了，好向下呼叫问路，却把身体虚弱的 Stefano 留在山上，让他自己找路下山。对吧？这根本是不可能完成的任务。

cues.en: So it's 08:30 in the morning. We find out for the first time that Stefano has not come down. The Italians have already tried to leave Camp 4, but are forced to come back up to us. It's a raging blizzard. We can't even see 10 feet out there. We have Libor. We look at each other and we say, they're right. Stefano is dead.
cues.zh: 早上8点半，我们第一次发现Stefano没有下来。意大利队员已经尝试离开四号营地，但被迫撤回我们这里。外面是猛烈的暴风雪。十英尺外什么都看不见。Libor也在。我们互相看看，说，他们说得对。Stefano死了。

cues.en: 36 year old man, his second attempt on K2,
cues.zh: 36岁的男子，第二次尝试攀登K2，

cues.en: he's been left by his partners, there's no chance for him now. When you are caught out in that extreme situation,
cues.zh: 他被同伴抛下了，现在他毫无机会。当你在那种极端情况下被困住时，

cues.en: you actually freeze solid at 40 below in six hours. So let's just pray that Stefano lay down in the snow,
cues.zh: 在零下40度，你其实六小时就会冻僵。所以我们只能祈祷Stefano是躺在雪里，

cues.en: and he just froze to death. His body will always be up there. That's what happens to you when you die up there. Like when you go to the summit of Mount Everest, you step over around seven dead bodies. There were people just like Stefano,
cues.zh: 然后就这么冻死了。他的遗体将永远留在那里。在那上面死掉就是这样。就像你去珠穆朗玛峰峰顶时，会跨过大约七具尸体。那里有和Stefano一样的人，

cues.en: who had a vision of themselves getting to the summit of Everest.
cues.zh: 他们曾憧憬自己登上珠峰之巅。

cues.en: They wanted so desperately to get a picture, and they died generally on the way down. So just like Stefano, those other seven people on Everest, when they find them and they go into their jacket, they're going to find a camera. And that camera is going to be a picture of them on the summit of Mount Everest, a picture that nobody will now will never see. They were so driven by their vision.
cues.zh: 他们拼了命想拍一张照片，而通常是在下山途中丧命。就像 Stefano 一样，珠峰上另外七个人，等人们找到他们、翻开他们的外套时，会发现一台相机。相机里会有一张他们在珠峰顶上的照片，一张现在再也不会有人看到的照片。他们被心中的那幅画面驱动得太深了。

cues.en: So here we are, we're trying to descend in this horrendous blizzard. We have Libor with us, we have the Italians with us, we have the Iranian climber with us. And I almost forgot to tell you this.
cues.zh: 就这样，我们正试图在这场可怕的暴风雪中下撤。我们身边有 Libor，有意大利人，还有那位伊朗登山者。我差点忘了告诉你们这件事。

cues.en: One of the other teams, not only did they, in a panicked state, leave Camp 4 to go back down, but they had lost one of their pairs of crampons.
cues.zh: 另一支队伍里，有人不仅在惊慌中离开4号营地往下撤，还丢了一副冰爪。

cues.en: Right? So you need the crampons to snap on the bottom of your feet to keep from slipping on the ice. So what we do is when we get in our tent, we sit on the front of our tent, we take the crampons off and leave them in this little room called a vestibule in the front of the tent. So what we do every day, do the same thing. The first guy gets in, he puts his crampons down, the second guy puts them on top, the third, and then we had a Liebhors, and then we had four pairs of crampons sitting in a pile. When we went to bed that night, we woke up in the morning, we only had three pairs of crampons.
cues.zh: 对吧？你需要把冰爪扣在鞋底，免得在冰面上打滑。所以我们进帐篷时，会坐在帐篷前部，把冰爪脱下来，放在帐篷前面一个叫前厅的小空间里。我们每天都这么做，流程一样。第一个人进去，把冰爪放下；第二个人叠在上面；第三个也是；然后轮到 Libor；最后四副冰爪堆成一堆。那晚睡下，第二天早上醒来，我们只剩三副冰爪了。

cues.en: Somebody else who lost their crampons had stolen the crampons out of front of our vestibule. So now we're descending. We're descending without a pair of crampons. Don says, you know what, I'll go down without the crampons. As he's descending, he hits a patch of ice just above Camp 3. He slides
cues.zh: 另一个丢了冰爪的人，把我们帐篷前厅门口的那副冰爪给偷走了。于是我们开始下撤。我们少了一副冰爪，就这么往下走。Don 说，这样吧，我不带冰爪下。下撤时，他在三号营地正上方踩到一片冰面，脚下一滑

cues.en: and tumbles towards Camp 3. By a miracle, he lands right side of the tent. But as he was tumbling, heard a snapping noise.
cues.zh: 一路翻滚着朝三号营地坠去。奇迹般地，他正好落在帐篷右边。可就在翻滚的时候，他听到一声脆响。

cues.en: And when he stands, his leg collapses.
cues.zh: 可他一站起来，那条腿就撑不住了。

cues.en: Here's a man at 24 and a half thousand feet in a horrible blizzard with a broken leg.
cues.zh: 这是一个身处两万四千五百英尺、遭遇可怕暴风雪、还断了腿的人。

cues.en: What are we going to do now? We have to get him down, we have to get Libor down, we have to get all of ourselves down. We are still, you know, two days from safety.
cues.zh: 现在该怎么办？我们必须把他弄下山，把Libor弄下山，把我们所有人都弄下山。你知道，我们离安全地带还有两天。

cues.en: We know we can't all make it to Camp 2. Libor can't make it to Camp 2. He's too physically destroyed.
cues.zh: 我们知道不可能所有人都到达2号营地。Libor到不了2号营地。他的身体已经垮得太厉害了。

cues.en: I'll stay at Camp 3 with Libor.
cues.zh: 我陪Libor留在3号营地。

cues.en: Don, you go down with the Italians, the Iranian and Bruce, and you guys can... They'll help you down, they'll get you to Camp 2. In Camp 2, we have a tent waiting for us with stove, fuel and a backup sleeping bag. So don't carry a sleeping bag, Don. Take the lightest pack you possibly can, right, because you've a broken leg, and start to go down. That's the plan when we leave.
cues.zh: Don，你跟意大利人、伊朗人和 Bruce 一起下撤，你们可以……他们会帮你下去，把你送到 2 号营地。2 号营地有顶帐篷等着我们，里面有炉子、燃料和备用睡袋。所以 Don，别带睡袋。尽量背最轻的包，明白吗，因为你腿断了，然后就开始下撤。我们出发时就这么计划。

cues.en: You know what happens as soon as they leave? The Italians in the Iranian race down to Camp 2.
cues.zh: 你知道他们一走会发生什么吗？意大利人和那个伊朗人会一路冲下 2 号营地。

cues.en: Bruce and Don slowly follow. They get into Camp 2 at 08:00 at night. They get to our tent at Camp 2.
cues.zh: Bruce和Don慢慢跟在后面。他们晚上8点到达2号营地。他们到了我们在2号营地的帐篷。

cues.en: Don opens the door to the tent, and in there is four people. It's a three person tent with four people. The Iranian and the three Italians are inside our tent.
cues.zh: Don打开帐篷门，里面有四个人。那是顶三人帐篷，却挤了四个人。那个伊朗人和三个意大利人在我们帐篷里。

cues.en: Mario
cues.zh: Mario

cues.en: is inside Don's sleeping bag.
cues.zh: 正躺在Don的睡袋里。

cues.en: Don goes, well, first of all, can I get in the tent? No, Don, there's no room for you in this tent. Well, why don't you guys stay in your own tent? Oh, somebody left the door open. It's filled with snow. It's destroyed now.
cues.zh: Don说，呃，首先，我能进帐篷吗？不行，Don，这帐篷里没你的地方。那你们怎么不住自己的帐篷？哦，有人没关帐篷门。里面灌满了雪。现在帐篷已经毁了。

cues.en: Maybe you could stay in our destroyed tent. Like, this is my tent. And Mario, that's my sleeping bag. And Mario goes to me, know what? Yesterday this was your sleeping bag, Don. Tomorrow this will be your sleeping bag. But today it is my sleeping bag. And he left Don to sit in the vestibulo tent for the whole night.
cues.zh: 也许你可以住我们那顶破帐篷。你看，这是我的帐篷。Mario，那是我的睡袋。Mario 对我说：你知道吗？昨天这是你的睡袋，Don；明天这还会是你的睡袋；但今天，它是我的睡袋。然后他就让 Don 在帐篷门厅里坐了一整夜。

cues.en: They wake up the next morning.
cues.zh: 第二天早上，他们醒了过来。

cues.en: Libor and I are coming from three. We get to two. We get to one. We finally catch up with Don and Bruce. As we are getting right to Advanced Base Camp, some Czech climbers have come around the corner to help us. We get back down to Advanced Base Camp. It's now 05:00 at night. It's impossible to carry Don in the remaining hour or so of sunlight back to base camp. So Don and I spend one more night in advanced base camp. We're laying in a tent next to each other. He's in extreme pain. We're calling up Johns Hopkins Hospital, some doctors know. We're trying to figure out what we can do for this guy. We're praying that the weather will break the next day, that they will bring a helicopter in. But no luck, it's socked in with clouds the next morning.

cues.zh: 第二个人死于试图去他的尸体旁，想把一具尸体从山坡上运下去，我觉得这简直太可怕了。救援的头号原则是：别害死救援者。所以当时就是这样：他们决定去救一具尸体，结果却在这个过程中害死了一个人，我觉得这正如我所说，是一场恐怖的事。

cues.en: Then they continued going to the summit and on the way back down.
cues.zh: 然后他们继续登顶，并在下山途中。

cues.en: One of them, a guy named Ralph Bay, who is a good friend of mine, an amazing mountaineer. He gets wiped away in an avalanche and when he is pulled off the mountain by the avalanche, he's connected to some rope. The anchors pull off the mountain and he pulls a key section of rope out with him. Right? His wife sees him fall to his death.
cues.zh: 其中一人叫 Ralph Bay，是我的好朋友，也是一位了不起的登山者。他被雪崩卷走，当雪崩把他从山上拖下去时，他身上连着绳子。锚点从山体上被拉脱，他也带着一段关键绳段一起被拽了下去。对吧？他的妻子眼睁睁看着他坠亡。

cues.en: She and her partner have a climbing rope in their pack and they take it out and they anchor it in, now they're able to rappel down off the steep section,
cues.zh: 她和同伴背包里带着一根攀岩绳，他们把它拿出来固定好，现在就能从陡峭路段绳降下去，

cues.en: and they are starting to traverse across. We don't know all the details, but it appears as if at least one other person coming down that rope afterwards
cues.zh: 然后他们开始横切过去。我们不清楚全部细节，但看起来后来至少有另一个人顺着那根绳下来

cues.en: thought it was connected to something and it wasn't. So it was just dangling in free air and rappelled right off the end of the rope. That was a guy named Yuges, who's a Frenchman who I was with as well in 2007.
cues.zh: 以为它连在什么东西上，其实并没有。结果绳子只是悬在半空，他一路绳降，直接从绳子末端滑了出去。那人叫Yuges，是个法国人，2007年我也曾和他同行。

cues.en: So, and then just all hell continues to break loose. In the end, 11 people die. It seems as if only one of them was an act of God that killed them. It seems as if the others were were... At least their deaths were compounded by a series of human errors. It was a horrible thing for me. In fact, it
cues.zh: 然后局面彻底失控。最终有11人丧生。看起来其中只有一人是死于天灾，其他人似乎……至少他们的死亡是由一连串人为失误叠加造成的。这对我来说太可怕了。事实上，那

cues.en: was a very devastating week for me to go through that whole thing. I couldn't believe it unfolded in the way that it did.
cues.zh: 整整一周经历这一切，对我来说是毁灭性的打击。我无法相信事情竟会以那样的方式展开。

cues.en: I think in some ways if you go back and analyze it, some of it was predictable.
cues.zh: 我觉得，某种程度上，如果回头分析一下，其中有些事是可以预料到的。

cues.en: In fact, it was so predictable
cues.zh: 事实上，它太可预料了，

cues.en: that one of the guys who was sending me emails back and forth kept saying, well, this sounds like the most dangerous part. I said to him the last email I sent says, no, you won't be killed there. The place that will kill you is ice coming off the
cues.zh: 以至于一直跟我来回发邮件的人里，有个家伙老说：嗯，这听起来像是最危险的部分。我跟他说，我最后一封邮件里写的是：不，你不会死在那儿。真正会要你命的地方，是从

cues.en: traverse, and that's exactly what killed this guy.
cues.zh: 横切段掉下来的冰，而这正是要了这家伙命的东西。

cues.zh: 这些演讲难道不是世界上最烂的营销工具吗？

cues.en: All right. Well, go to work. Have fun.
cues.zh: 好了，那就去工作吧，玩得开心。
